The graph of $y = g(x) + 17$ is shown. Which equation defines function $g$?
explanation: Choice A is correct. The equation of the line shown can be written in slope-intercept form $y = mx + b$. The y-intercept of the graph is $(0, -1)$, so $b = -1$. The line also passes through $(3, 0)$, so the slope is $\frac{0 - (-1)}{3 - 0} = \frac{1}{3}$. Therefore, an equation of the graph is $y = \frac{1}{3}x - 1$. Since the graph represents $y = g(x) + 17$, substituting $g(x) + 17$ for $y$ gives $g(x) + 17 = \frac{1}{3}x - 1$. Subtracting $17$ from both sides yields $g(x) = \frac{1}{3}x - 18$.
